steps.what: Identify replacement parts and confirm compatibility and required quantity
Enter verified replacement parts into a draft order
Check delivery and commercial terms and place the parts order

tasks.design: Use the {OTHER} asset service system to identify equipment and capture a verified request, then populate a draft in {PROCUREMENT}. The installer checks compatibility, substitutions, price and delivery and places the exact approved order.
tasks.previous_blocker: A verified part request is often entered again into purchasing screens.
tasks.enabler_now: Native request-to-order configuration can copy identifiers and quantities without choosing substitute parts.
tasks.still_hard: Obsolete components, firmware compatibility and substitute approvals.
tasks.human_edge: Know whether the proposed component is suitable for the installed alarm system.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry; technical and purchasing authority remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Populating an order from a verified parts request is a plausible configuration; no measured alarm installer purchasing case is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary begins after fault diagnosis and includes parts selection, request capture and order placement, excluding physical repair and supplier fulfilment.

Installer produces asset reference, manufacturer part reference, compatible specification version, quantity, unit, supplier, price and delivery location/date in s1. Capture and missing-field clarification retain all 45 hours.
Test native request-to-order configuration first. Missing identifiers or substitutes require manual selection and entry; s2 cannot infer compatibility.
Four focal upkeep hours and two purchasing-team mapping hours are additional ongoing effort.
unknowns: Catalogue quality and proportion of obsolete parts
research_questions: How much order effort is duplicate entry after all compatibility fields are captured?

already_counted.description: Compatibility checks and verified request capture

incremental.description: Purchasing catalogue and field mapping upkeep

approvals.approved_version: Exact asset, part specification, supplier, quantity, price and delivery details; substitutions void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=45+0+25=70, gross=30, focal upkeep=4, net=26. High assumes a genuine duplicate-entry component and complete verified requests; low retains all manual entry for obsolete or unstructured requests plus upkeep.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Reconcile service facts and document requirements for invoices or warranties
Prepare invoice or warranty documents from verified service facts
Check invoice or warranty wording and release the final documents

tasks.design: Generate documents from verified fields in the {OTHER} field service system using approved {DOCS} templates. The installer retains service reconciliation and final release; invoice arithmetic is deterministic and warranty entitlement is not inferred.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same service and equipment facts are retyped into customer documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field service document generation already supports converting work orders into invoices.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed hours, contractual exceptions and warranty eligibility.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the work and recognise unsupported charges or warranty promises.
tasks.altitude: Less document assembly; no change to release rights or physical work.

reach.learn: Trace charges and warranty terms to approved service evidence

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy supports work orders, asset management and automatic work-order-to-invoice conversion.
Warranty template population and the proposed assembly saving are unmeasured design assumptions; automated warranty entitlement is not established.

assumptions: Boundary is installer document preparation and release, excluding repair, payment collection and any invoice assembly already owned by finance; allocate that action once in roll-ups.

Installer produces verified asset/serial reference, customer, work date, hours, parts, rates, tax treatment, applicable warranty terms/version and document type in s1's full 35 hours. Missing facts return to manual reconciliation, not inferred fields.
Commercial staff maintain approved template and rate versions through existing processes; additional maintenance is counted. Test native field service templates before custom code.
Five additional focal hours cover exception handling and document samples; three other-role hours cover rate and template upkeep.
unknowns: Who currently prepares and releases documents
Native invoice and warranty template support
research_questions: Does generation remove retyping after source capture, reconciliation and customer-document checks?

Meaning, charges and warranty review before release

incremental.description: Document samples and exceptional generation failures

approvals.approved_version: Exact document, customer, asset, charges, tax fields and warranty terms version; changes void release approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+20=55, gross=45, focal upkeep=5, net=40. High requires repetitive document assembly from a complete verified brief; low assumes bespoke warranty disputes require manual writing plus upkeep. No repair or supplier saving enters the estimate.
